title: MovenRun documentation
description: MovenRun is a movement game. Cover ground on a map, claim a cell each session, and keep it by coming back. What the app does today, and what is planned.
headings: What is in the app today
keywords: movenrun movenrun is a movement game. you walk, run or cycle, and the ground you cover becomes territory on a map. each session claims a cell. coming back is what keeps it. how a session works what you press, what the screen shows, what happens when you stop. capture and the map the cell grid, and what one session actually claims. holding your ground how a hold fades, and what returning does. the loop each session runs the loop once. move, and the app records your route. save the session, and the first cell on that route you did not already hold becomes yours. walk the same ground again and your hold on it firms up. leave it alone and the hold fades on its own. pace does not come into it. a short walk you actually repeat beats a long run you do once, which is the whole point of the design. what is in the app today movement sessions, capture, holding and decay, districts and mastery, xp, levels, streaks and collections all work. so does the route checking that decides whether a session counts. clubs and the city layer are in the app as a local preview built from seeded data. they do not sync between players yet. points and deeds are designed and not built. each page says which of these it is describing. where to start to understand the game, read how a session works , then capture and holding . to understand what keeps it fair, read movement verification . to understand what is coming, read points , deeds and onchain , and the roadmap .

title: How a session works
description: What happens in a MovenRun session: starting, what the screen shows while you move, finishing, and what saving does.
keywords: how a session works a session is one walk, run or ride. you start it, you move, you finish, and you decide whether to save it. nothing is recorded until you save. starting before anything begins, the app checks whether it can read your location and tells you plainly what it found. if access has not been granted it asks. if it was refused earlier, or location is switched off on the device, the screen says which of those it is and takes you to the right settings page. location is read only while a session is running, in the foreground. there is no background tracking, and the app does not record where you are between sessions. if you cannot or would rather not share location, a demo route is available. it draws a synthetic loop so you can see how the screens behave. it is labelled as a demo throughout and it never counts for anything. while you move the route draws itself as you go. above it sit three numbers: distance, elapsed time and current pace. that is the whole screen, deliberately, so there is nothing worth looking down at. a signal indicator shows whether the app has a good fix, a weak one, or is still searching. weak signal does not stop the session, it just tells you why the line might wander. you can pause and resume as often as you like. paused time does not count toward your total. nothing needs a tap while you are actually moving. finishing finishing asks you to confirm, so a session cannot end by accident, and the same confirmation catches the back button. once confirmed, the app works out what the session was worth and shows you a summary before anything is written down. the summary carries the route, the distance, the time, the pace, which cells you crossed, and a score for how clean the gps signal was. see movement verification for what that score means. saving saving is a separate, deliberate press. until you press it, the session has changed nothing. a session has to cover 200 metres or last five minutes before it can be saved. below that the summary explains why the button is not there. saving does three things at once. it banks the xp for the session, it claims one new cell, and it refreshes your hold on any cells you already held and crossed. the detail of the second and third is in capture and the map and holding your ground . one saved session a day only the first session you save each day earns xp or affects the map. later sessions still record and still show you a summary, and they bank nothing. this is a deliberate ceiling. it means the game cannot be won by having a free afternoon, and it means a person with twenty spare minutes a day is competitive with anyone.

title: Capture and the map
description: How a MovenRun route becomes claimed ground: the hexagonal cell grid, what one session claims, and what the map shows you afterwards.
keywords: capture and the map finishing a session turns part of your route into ground you hold. one cell per session, and the map keeps the record. the cell grid the map is a grid of hexagons. every point on it falls inside exactly one cell, and a cell is the smallest piece of ground you can hold. hexagons rather than squares because each one borders six neighbours at an equal distance. ground spreads outward evenly, and there are no awkward diagonal corners where two cells meet at a point. cells in the current build are roughly 300 metres across. the grid is generated on your device, so the same street always resolves to the same cell for you. moving to a shared global grid, where the same corner is the same cell for every player, is planned and is what districts and clubs are waiting on. what one session claims a session claims the first cell on your route that you did not already hold. your route passes through a run of cells. when you save the session, the app walks that list in order and claims the first one you do not already hold. that is one new cell per saved session, however far you went. the rest of the touched cells are not wasted. any that you already hold have their hold refreshed, which is the main way ground stays yours. a long route through your own neighbourhood might claim nothing new and still be the most useful session of the week. a session has to cover 200 metres or last five minutes before it can be saved at all. below that it is treated as noise rather than a walk. one claim a day saving is limited to one session per calendar day. a second session that day still records and still shows you its summary, and it will not claim a cell or refresh a hold. the limit exists so the map rewards a habit rather than an afternoon. someone who walks once a day for a month ends up with far more ground than someone who walks six times on a sunday. what the map shows the territory map is the running record of everything you hold. each cell is drawn in the state it is currently in, so you can see at a glance which ground is solid and which needs a visit. what each cell state means on the map state what it means yours held and defended. nothing needed. at risk your hold has drained low. a visit restores it. contested left long enough that the hold is gone and your grip is slipping. dormant neglected long enough to drop off. walking it again brings it back. tapping a cell opens its detail view: how long you have held it, when you were last there, how strong your hold is, and what to do next. the numbers behind those states are set out in holding your ground . cell names cells carry short names like riverside loop or signal yard. they are generated from the cell's own identifier, so a given cell always shows the same name and it stays the same for as long as you hold it. they are labels for your own map rather than real place names, which is deliberate: the app never resolves your position to a real address, neighbourhood or landmark.

title: Holding your ground
description: How a MovenRun cell stays yours: the defense and control meters, how fast a hold fades, and what returning and fortifying do.
keywords: holding your ground claiming a cell is the easy part. every cell you hold has a grip that loosens while you stay away, and walking it again is what tightens it. two meters each cell you hold carries two numbers. defense is the buffer, and it starts at 40 out of 100 the moment you claim the cell. control is your actual grip, and it starts full at 100. defense drains by 12 points a day from your last visit. control does not move at all while defense has anything left in it. only once defense reaches zero does control start dropping, and then only by 6 points a day. the effect is a grace period. a freshly claimed cell has a bit over three days before your grip starts loosening, and a cell you visit regularly never loses any grip at all. visiting the cell resets both. what the states mean those two numbers put every cell into one of four states, which is what the map colours. only time away moves a cell down this list. the four states a held cell can be in state when what it means held defense above 25 solid. nothing needed. at risk defense below 25 the buffer is nearly gone. one visit refills it. contested defense at zero for about six days the buffer has run out and your hold is fading. a visit still recovers it. dormant control below 35, or twelve days away the cell has dropped off your active map. walking it again brings it back. contested is a description of your own neglect rather than of anything happening around you. nobody takes a cell off you in movenrun. time is the only thing that moves a cell down this list, and a visit is the only thing that moves it back up. returning when you save a session, every cell you already held that your route crossed gets refreshed automatically. defense goes up by 40 and control by 10, both capped at 100, and the clock starts again from that moment. that is the main way ground stays yours, and it costs nothing beyond going for the walk. a regular route through your own neighbourhood keeps a dozen cells permanently solid without you ever thinking about it. fortifying fortifying is the deliberate version. from a cell's detail view you can add 25 to its defense without going anywhere, once per cell per day. it is free. fortifying tops up the buffer and nothing else, so it buys time rather than grip. it is what you reach for when you know you will be away for a while. bringing a dormant cell back a dormant cell is not lost. it sits on your map in a faded state, and the next session whose route crosses it picks it straight back up. long absences cost you position, not history.

title: Districts and clubs
description: How MovenRun cells feed districts, what mastering a district takes, and what the club and city layer is today.
keywords: districts and clubs above individual cells sit districts, and above districts sits a city layer. the first is in the app. the second is a preview. districts there are eight districts, with fixed names: north loop, glass quarter, signal yard, riverline, pulse market, beacon park, volt junction and dawn grid. they are a flavour layer rather than places. each cell you hold is assigned to one of the eight by its own identifier, so the grouping is stable and repeatable, and a district is not an area of your city. nothing about a district reflects where you actually went. that is deliberate, and it is the same reason cells carry invented names rather than street names. districts are eight fixed names, not map areas. district status a district takes its status from the cells inside it. a district with no cells is locked. one cell makes it emerging, two or more in good standing make it controlled, and a district holding cells that are at risk or dormant shows as needing attention. the city view sorts your districts by which of them needs a visit most, so the app can answer the only question that matters on the way out of the door. mastery mastery is the long arc. each district carries a score built from how much of it you control, how well defended those cells are, how consistently you have been moving, and how clean your recent gps signal has been. the score sorts a district into one of five bands: discovered, rising, fortified, and signature at the top, with locked for districts you have not reached. getting to signature takes sustained holding rather than a single good week. clubs, as a preview clubs are a local preview. the club list in the app is seeded data. the rival figures are fixed numbers rather than other people's activity, and nothing syncs between players. your own club figures are real, because they are built from your own stats. the design is that joining a club pools the ground its members hold, and clubs then compete over districts across a season. the city view in the app shows the shape of that: a season board, district standing, and pressure on the districts you hold least well. making it real needs shared state between players, which is the next substantial piece of work. until then the club layer is best read as a mockup you can walk around in. the roadmap puts it directly after the movement game.

title: Tasks, streaks and levels
description: XP, levels, streaks, daily tasks and collections in MovenRun, and how movement and tasks share one daily allowance.
headings: One award per thing per day
keywords: tasks, streaks and levels alongside the map there is a straightforward progression layer. all of it is in the app and all of it is local to your device. xp and levels a saved session earns xp based on what you actually did: 60 for each kilometre and 3 for each minute, added together. the result is floored at 25, so a short walk is still worth banking, and capped at 300, so a very long session cannot run away with it. levels are a flat curve. every 500 xp is one level, with no acceleration and no rubber-banding. the profile screen shows how far through the current level you are. daily tasks there are five short exercise tasks in the app: a cardio burst, a mobility flow, a core circuit, a breathing reset and a stair climb. each runs on a timer between one and two minutes and carries its own xp value, between 60 and 180. one of the five is featured each day, rotating at local midnight, and the rest stay available. they are bodyweight exercises rather than movement sessions, so they are something to do on a day you are not going out. one award per thing per day every task, and the movement session itself, awards xp at most once per local day. repeating something the same day still works and simply banks nothing further. movement sessions run through the same daily gate as the tasks, which is why only the first saved session of a day counts. it is one consistent rule rather than two separate systems. streaks your streak counts consecutive days on which you finished something. complete anything today after having completed something yesterday and it goes up by one. miss a day and it resets to one on your next active day. only the first completion of a day moves the streak, so there is nothing to farm. collections collections are badges grouped into six sets, covering first steps, holding territory, defending it, gps signal quality, joining a club, and mapping. each badge tracks a real count from your own play and shows how far along it is. they are a record of what you have done rather than something to spend. nothing in the app is gated behind a badge. weekly recap the recap looks back over a rolling seven days and summarises your sessions, the ground you took and refreshed, and how your signal quality trended. it is built from what the app already stores, and it contains no coordinates, no route paths and no place names.

title: Movement verification
description: How MovenRun checks that a route really happened, what gets rejected, and why no coordinates are stored.
keywords: movement verification a game about covering ground has to know the ground was covered. it does not have to know where you live, and movenrun is built so it cannot. why routes get checked if a route that never happened could claim a cell, holding one would mean nothing, and the people it would stop rewarding first are the ones actually walking. checking routes is what makes the map worth playing on. what gets checked every route runs all four checks. speed. a route has to move at speeds a person moves at. anything implying a vehicle is thrown out. accuracy. individual positions that are too imprecise are dropped, and a route made mostly of poor fixes is rejected rather than guessed at. continuity. a route needs enough positions, close enough together in time, to describe someone actually travelling. a jump across town does not pass. not a repeat. each route reduces to a fingerprint. submitting the same movement twice is caught, as is a route overlapping one already counted. the signal score every finished session gets a score out of 100 for how clean its gps was, along with the reasons behind it. steady accuracy, a realistic pace and a good density of positions push it up. weak signal, sparse positions or a speed spike pull it down, and the summary names which applied. the score is feedback rather than a gate. it does not change your xp, does not decide whether a cell is claimed, and does not affect anything you hold. it is there so you can tell the difference between a quiet session and a phone that had a bad time in a tunnel. over several sessions those scores build into a readiness view, which is a trend line rather than a verdict. your coordinates are not stored this is the part worth being exact about. while a session runs, your positions live in memory on your device. they are used for two things: working out whether the movement was plausible, and working out which cells you crossed. when you leave the summary they are gone. what is kept afterwards is the distance, the duration, which cells you touched, the signal score and its reasons. no latitude or longitude is written down at any point, so there is no history of where you went for anyone to read, lose or hand over. the fingerprint used to catch repeats is derived from the route and cannot be turned back into one. the same rule holds everywhere else in the app. cell names are invented rather than looked up, districts are assigned by identifier rather than by location, and the weekly recap is built from counts. nothing in movenrun resolves your position to a real address, neighbourhood or landmark. where the checking runs today the checks run on your device, which is also why everything above stays there. a server-side version of the same pipeline is built and is planned to run alongside it, so that what counts toward a shared map is verified somewhere a device cannot influence. it is not connected to the app yet.

title: Points
description: Points are the planned in-game currency in MovenRun: what would earn them, what they would be spent on, and what they are not.
headings: What they would be spent on
keywords: points points are the planned in-game currency. they are not in the app, and this page describes a design rather than something you can hold. what points are for an in-game currency with no monetary value. the intent is a single in-game currency that connects moving to holding. saving a session is designed to earn points. spending them is designed to strengthen ground you already hold, so that a cell you have invested in fades more slowly than one you have not. that gives the map a second lever. today the only way to keep ground is to walk it. with points there would also be a way to prepare for a week when you know you cannot. what would earn them the same things that already earn xp: saving a movement session, and completing the daily tasks. points are designed to sit alongside xp rather than replace it, with xp tracking how far you have come and points being something you spend. what they would be spent on fortifying a cell beyond what the free daily action gives. strengthening a district you are working toward mastering. entering the seasonal city play once clubs sync between players. what points are not points have no monetary value. they cannot be bought, sold, cashed out or exchanged, and they are not designed to become any of those things later. there is no purchase anywhere in movenrun and none is planned. points and deeds are separate. a deed records which cells you hold. points are spent inside the game. neither is a holding of value. when points come after clubs sync between players, because a currency is only interesting once there is something shared to spend it against. the order is in the roadmap .

title: Deeds and onchain
description: Zone Deeds are the planned onchain record of which cells a player holds. What a deed would record, and where the contracts run today.
keywords: deeds and onchain movenrun's contracts run on base sepolia while the design is tested. mainnet at launch. what a deed is one deed per cell. a record of standing, nothing more. a zone deed is a durable record of a cell you hold. one deed per cell. it records which cell, who holds it, and how long they have held it, and it is kept under the holder's own keys rather than in an account somebody else controls. what a deed is for is permanence. everything you build in movenrun today lives on your device, and a deed is how a long-held cell becomes a record that outlasts a reinstall. a record of standing a deed is a record of standing in a game. it is not property, it is not an investment, and it is not designed to carry value. holding one says you have held that cell, and nothing else. length of holding is the thing a deed is designed to make legible. ground held for a year reads differently from ground claimed last week, and that difference is the only ranking a deed expresses. where the contracts are the contracts are deployed to base sepolia, which is a test network, while the design is worked through. nothing has been issued on them. addresses go up at mainnet launch, alongside the deed registry itself. wallets holding a deed needs somewhere to keep it. the intent is that this is arranged for you and stays out of the way, so that the game does not begin with a setup task. that work has not started and no provider has been chosen. until it does, movenrun asks nothing of you on this front. there is no wallet in the app and nothing to connect. deeds and points these are separate designs. points are an in-game currency for strengthening ground. a deed is a record of which ground you hold. neither converts into the other, and neither carries monetary value.

title: Roadmap
description: What is built in MovenRun and what comes next: the movement game, clubs syncing between players, Points, and deeds on Base.
keywords: roadmap the game first, then the layers on top of it. that ordering decides everything below. order matters more than dates here. 1 · the movement game sessions, capture, the hold and decay model, districts and mastery, xp, levels, streaks and collections, and the route checking behind all of it. status: built. this is what the app does today. 2 · clubs and city play clubs sync between players, so the ground a club holds is a real shared total and the season board reflects other people rather than seeded figures. this needs shared state, which is the largest single piece of work on this list. status: planned. the club and city screens exist in the app as a local preview. 3 · points the in-game currency arrives: earned by moving, spent on strengthening ground. it comes after clubs because a currency needs something shared to be spent against. see points . status: planned. not in the app. 4 · deeds on base the deed registry moves to base mainnet and held ground starts becoming a durable record kept under your own keys. contract addresses are published at that point. see deeds and onchain . status: planned. the contracts are on a test network while the design is worked through. how this changes phases move when the previous one holds up, rather than on a date. the game has to be worth playing before anything is worth building on top of it, and the route checking has to be sound before it decides anything shared. this page is updated as that happens.

title: Frequently asked questions
description: Straight answers about MovenRun: how ground is claimed and kept, what happens to your location data, and what is built versus planned.
headings: Do I have to be fast?
How much do I claim per session?
What happens to my location data?
Does it track me in the background?
Do I need to know anything about crypto?
keywords: frequently asked questions straight answers about what movenrun is and how much of it exists. what is movenrun? a movement game. you walk, run or cycle, and the ground your route covers becomes cells you hold on a map. keep visiting and the ground stays yours. do i have to be fast? no, and the design works against it. ground is kept by returning rather than by pace or distance, only the first saved session each day counts, and xp is capped. a twenty minute walk every morning beats one long weekend run. how much do i claim per session? one cell. saving a session claims the first cell on your route that you did not already hold, however far you went. cells you already held and crossed get their hold refreshed at the same time. see capture and the map . can i lose ground? your hold on a cell fades while you stay away, and a cell left long enough goes dormant and drops off your active map. walking it again brings it back. no other player can take a cell from you. see holding your ground . what happens to my location data? your positions are used during a session to check the movement was plausible and to work out which cells you crossed, and then they are gone. no latitude or longitude is stored. what is kept is distance, duration, which cells you touched, and a signal score. see movement verification . does it track me in the background? no. location is read only while a session is running and only in the foreground. what stops people faking movement? every route is checked for plausible speed, usable accuracy and continuous motion, and any route that repeats one already counted is rejected. see movement verification . do i need to know anything about crypto? no. there is no wallet in the app and nothing to connect. deeds are a planned layer and are described in deeds and onchain . is there anything to buy? no. there is no purchase anywhere in movenrun and none is planned. what are points worth? points are a planned in-game currency for strengthening ground you hold. they have no monetary value and cannot be exchanged for anything outside the game. see points . are clubs real? not yet. the club and city screens are a local preview built from seeded data and do not sync between players. making them real is the next phase. see districts and clubs . what is actually built? built: movement sessions, capture, holding and decay, districts and mastery, xp, levels, streaks, collections, the weekly recap, and route checking. a local preview: clubs, the city season board, rivals and sponsor zones. planned: points, deeds, and wallets. the roadmap gives the order.

title: Disclaimers
description: Important notices about MovenRun: a pre-launch product, Points have no monetary value, not financial advice, not a medical device, and how location data is handled.
headings: Points and deeds have no monetary value

documentation describes the product as designed and as currently built, and it says on each page which of the two it means. features, numbers and timing may change, and anything described as planned may change substantially or not ship. nothing here is a commitment to deliver a specific feature on a specific date. points and deeds have no monetary value points are a planned in-game currency. they have no monetary value, cannot be exchanged for cash or cryptocurrency, and cannot be bought or sold. zone deeds are a planned record of which cells a player holds and are likewise not a holding of value. there is no purchase in movenrun. not financial advice nothing in this documentation is financial, investment, legal or tax advice, and nothing here is an offer, a solicitation or an invitation to invest. movenrun makes no promise of profit, income, return or appreciation of any kind. not a medical device movenrun supports walking, running and cycling. it is not a medical device, it gives no location is read only while a session is running, and only while the app is in the foreground. positions are used to check the movement was plausible and to work out which cells the route crossed, and
